messages:
maria: Heads-up — I'm proposing a 'clustered entitlement decomposition' approach for the quarterly access review. Instead of sweeping org-wide, we group related admin grants into clusters (billing, infra, model-serving, kms). Reason: reduces blast radius and makes owners actionable.
kevin: +1 conceptually. how do you plan to identify clusters? tags, resource prefixes, or heuristic?
sasha: tagging is spotty; prefixes for infra/model-serving ok, but billing is scattered. Could we augment with last-used telemetry?
maria: plan: 1) start with tags/prefixes, 2) cross-ref with audit-logs for last API usage, 3) run a short-lived canary automation to set expirations on a handful of non-prod admin grants.
ryan: for step 2 can you paste the audit query? I can help run it for prod staging.
maria: sure — using our internal ELK: 
```
GET /redwood-audit-*/_search
{
  "query": { "bool": { "must": [ {"term": {"principal":"SERVICE_ACCOUNT:svc-analytics"}}, {"range": {"@timestamp": {"gte": "now-90d"}}} ] } }
}
```
kevin: nice. we'll need to map service accounts to owners; svcacct metadata is incomplete in some repos. can we use KMS grant metadata instead?
sasha: KMS grants have labels. we can use grant tags + key arn prefix to cluster kms-admins by product. also check CMKs with high-use patterns.
maria: agree. also thinking of adding a short-lived automation that: creates a ticket, adds owners, and sets entitlement expiry to 7d for canary batch. If nobody claims, entitlement is downgraded to read-only.
access-bot: Automated run scheduled: canary_entitlement_batch #7 at 1798883600. Results will post to #eng-security. :robot_face:
ashley: question on service-roles used by infra pipelines — if we set expiry, will pipelines break? we need a safety net.
ryan: we can add a 'pipeline-exempt' cluster that requires manual opt-in; also we should implement a fallback policy: on failing auth we auto-escalate to dedicated infra pool for 30m while owner is paged.
kevin: paging owners is fine but we must log escalations to audit with correlation id. otherwise we lose evidence for compliance.
sasha: add KMS change hook: any automated entitlement downgrade on key-admin should emit KMS event and create a ledger entry. small code snippet: 
```
emit_event({"actor":"entitlement-automation","action":"downgrade","key":key_arn,"correlation_id":cid})
```
maria: action items: 1) kevin + sasha: draft clustering heuristics and sample queries (due EOD Thu), 2) ryan + ashley: list pipeline service-accounts to exempt, 3) i’ll draft canary runbook and rollback playbook.
kevin: I'll take cluster heuristics. also will prototype an owner backfill script that looks up git commits and deploy manifests to guess owners.
ashley: I'll collate pipeline accounts and run a smoke test for one staging pipeline if you need.
ryan: agree to meet Wed 10am to walk through the canary runbook. please @mention me in the runbook PR.
maria: thanks all. tagging follow-ups into the access review board doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/access-reviews#clustered-decomposition (WIP).
kevin: small nit — add a field in tickets for 'compliance-proof' to attach audit extracts.
maria: will do. if no blockers I'll schedule the canary for next Tue and run with access-bot. :thumbsup:
